title: Yara and the Verdict
premise: Orsen Coldharbour has spent a decade as the unseen voice on the night radio of Coldharbour Cabs, logging every ride, every argument, every secret that passes through the back seat. When a drowned man is found wearing clothes lifted from Orsen's own closet, the police fixate on them, and Orsen realizes the victim was a childhood friend who vanished thirty years ago—the same night Orsen's memory goes blank. Following dispatch logs and taxi receipts like breadcrumbs, Orsen uncovers that the town's beloved founding families staged an accident decades ago and have been paying for silence ever since. In the end, Orsen chooses testimony over invisibility, exposing the verdict that was buried and finally claiming a place among the found family of witnesses who refuse to look away.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is the pen name of a former small-town radio operator who spent years listening to strangers confess between fare announcements. They write mysteries about people who know too much by accident.

chapters.title: The Clothes in My Closet
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A drowned body surfaces in the reservoir wearing Orsen's missing jacket and scarf, and Detective Ilsa Vann treats them as suspect rather than witness. Searching their apartment, Orsen finds a thirty-year-old photograph tucked in the jacket lining showing themselves and a boy named Tam—whose face matches the dead man. The beat is dread: the past has broken into the present.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with interludes from dispatcher trainee Nia, who becomes an unlikely ally. Pulling ten years of night-shift logs, Orsen maps rides connecting the victim to the Ashcombe family estate on the anniversary of a 1994 drowning ruled accidental. Each log entry contradicts the official story. The beat is compulsion: Orsen can't stop reading their own records as evidence.

chapters.title: The Verdict Before the Verdict
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Lured to the reservoir at night by a fake dispatch call, Orsen confronts matriarch Corla Ashcombe, who reveals Tam was her grandson and the 1994 'accident' a cover-up she's protected ever since—and that Orsen witnessed it as a child, which is why their memory fractured. When Vann arrives, Orsen must decide whether to run or speak. The beat is the climax: choosing voice over erasure.

chapters.title: What the Night Radio Heard
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, closing with Nia's first solo shift. Testimony given, the town convulses, but Orsen gains something unexpected: Vann's grudging respect, Nia's friendship, and a recovered fragment of the lost night—Tam's hand pulling them toward the water, trying to save them both. The beat is belonging: invisibility traded for witness, and a found family formed in its place.
